reason: The text demonstrates that non-leaders exercise agency throughout. Moses, who is not yet a leader but a fugitive, independently decides to intervene on behalf of the priest's daughters—he 'rose up' (וַיָּ֤קָם) and rescued them from the shepherds without any authority or appointment. The seven daughters themselves demonstrate considerable agency: they independently drew water, filled the troughs, and managed their father's flock. They also made autonomous decisions (returning to the well, speaking to their father, later going to call Moses). Even the shepherds exercise agency in their antagonistic actions. The passage shows multiple levels of agent actors—not merely hierarchical leaders—making decisions and taking actions that drive the narrative forward.
